SALIM.who: Salim, 34, toll booth operator, 2001. Narration: flat, matter-of-fact, Indian English; live lines quieter, unsettled.

MRS. IYER.who: Mrs. Iyer, 60s, South Indian, warm, chatty, tired.

SECRETARY.who: Society secretary, 50s, woken at 3 AM, irritated then frightened. Landline phone.

MAA.who: Nikhil's mother, 50s, on the phone from home town: loving, worried, Hindi-English mix.

RAGHU (V.O.).who: Raghu, 52, night watchman, Mumbai 1998. Narrates from beyond (already dead): calm, low, tired, Indian English, slow. Live lines in the tape: plain, a little nervous.

SALIM (V.O.).who: Salim, 34, toll booth operator, 2001. Narration: flat, matter-of-fact, Indian English; live lines quieter, unsettled.

MR. DESHMUKH.who: Mr. Deshmukh, 70s, retired, polite, too calm. Knows things he shouldn't.

lines.speaker: RAGHU (V.O.)
lines.text: My name was Raghu. In March of '98, I took the night shift at Shanti Vihar.
lines.speak: My name was Raghu. In March of '98, I took the night shift at Shanti Vihar.

lines.speaker: RAGHU (V.O.)
lines.text: The old watchman, Kishan, had stopped coming. Nobody told me why.
lines.speak: The old watchman, Kishan, had stopped coming. Nobody told me why.

lines.speaker: RAGHU (V.O.)
lines.text: Four buildings, one gate, one register. It was supposed to be easy work.
lines.speak: Four buildings, one gate, one register. It was supposed to be easy work.

lines.speaker: RAGHU (V.O.)
lines.text: I wrote my name in the register. Raghu, ten-forty PM. Neat letters. My father taught me that.
lines.speak: I wrote my name in the register. Raghu, ten-forty PM. Neat letters. My father taught me that.

lines.speaker: RAGHU (V.O.)
lines.text: Someone had cut his face out of it. I told myself it was the society children.
lines.speak: Someone had cut his face out of it. I told myself it was the society children.

lines.speaker: RAGHU (V.O.)
lines.text: He knew my name before I said it. Old men in old buildings know everything. That's what I told myself.
lines.speak: He knew my name before I said it. Old men in old buildings know everything. That's what I told myself.

lines.speaker: RAGHU (V.O.)
lines.text: Four terraces, four padlocks. I counted the keys twice. I don't know why.
lines.speak: Four terraces, four padlocks. I counted the keys twice. I don't know why.

lines.speaker: RAGHU (V.O.)
lines.text: I stood under that balcony a long time. Long enough to feel foolish. Not long enough to leave.
lines.speak: I stood under that balcony a long time. Long enough to feel foolish. Not long enough to leave.

lines.speaker: RAGHU (V.O.)
lines.text: Eight months of dust. And a clock on the wall, stopped at twelve minutes past three.
lines.speak: Eight months of dust. And a clock on the wall, stopped at twelve minutes past three.

lines.speaker: RAGHU (V.O.)
lines.text: Every place I had been that night, someone had written it down. To the minute.
lines.speak: Every place I had been that night, someone had written it down. To the minute.

lines.speaker: RAGHU (V.O.)
lines.text: I didn't look behind me. I have thought about that a lot, since.
lines.speak: I didn't look behind me. I have thought about that a lot, since.

lines.speaker: RAGHU
lines.text: Going out, sahab? I kept it open, like you asked.
lines.speak: Going out, sahab? I kept it open, like you asked.

lines.speaker: RAGHU
lines.text: Sahab, the gate stays locked after—
lines.speak: Sahab, the gate stays locked after—

lines.speaker: RAGHU
lines.text: Deshmukh-ji? Sahab... at this hour?
lines.speak: Deshmukh-ji? Sahab... at this hour?

lines.speaker: RAGHU (V.O.)
lines.text: He didn't answer. He didn't even look at me.
lines.speak: He didn't answer. He didn't even look at me.

lines.speaker: RAGHU
lines.text: ...That's not my handwriting.
lines.speak: ...That's not my handwriting.

lines.speaker: RAGHU (V.O.)
lines.text: The first round was quiet. The first round always is.
lines.speak: The first round was quiet. The first round always is.

lines.speaker: RAGHU (V.O.)
lines.text: Around three, I sat down to write the round in the register.
lines.speak: Around three, I sat down to write the round in the register.

lines.speaker: RAGHU (V.O.)
lines.text: Then the power went. The whole society, all at once.
lines.speak: Then the power went. The whole society, all at once.

lines.speaker: MR. DESHMUKH
lines.text: Watchman-ji.
lines.speak: Watchman-ji.

lines.speaker: MRS. IYER
lines.text: Watchman-ji? Are you there?
lines.speak: Watchman-ji? Are you there?

lines.speaker: SALIM (V.O.)
lines.text: Salim. Thirty-four. Night booth at the NH-4 toll plaza. November, 2001.
lines.speak: Salim. Thirty-four. Night booth at the NH-4 toll plaza. November, 2001.

lines.speaker: SALIM (V.O.)
lines.text: Nobody drives that road after one. That's why they gave the night to me.
lines.speak: Nobody drives that road after one. That's why they gave the night to me.

lines.speaker: SALIM (V.O.)
lines.text: Take the money, tear the receipt, write the plate, lift the arm. That was the whole job.
lines.speak: Take the money, tear the receipt, write the plate, lift the arm. That was the whole job.

lines.speaker: SALIM (V.O.)
lines.text: Bombay plate. MH 04 AX 0312. An old man driving. Exact change. He never looked at me.
lines.speak: Bombay plate. MH 04 AX 0312. An old man driving. Exact change. He never looked at me.

lines.speaker: SALIM (V.O.)
lines.text: Same van. Same plate. The driver was young this time. Younger than me.
lines.speak: Same van. Same plate. The driver was young this time. Younger than me.

lines.speaker: SALIM (V.O.)
lines.text: He was wearing my uniform. My name badge. I checked my own shirt. It was still on me.
lines.speak: He was wearing my uniform. My name badge. I checked my own shirt. It was still on me.

lines.speaker: SALIM (V.O.)
lines.text: Four of them in the back now. The one by the window wore a watchman's khaki. He never blinked.
lines.speak: Four of them in the back now. The one by the window wore a watchman's khaki. He never blinked.

lines.speaker: SALIM (V.O.)
lines.text: I never wrote that line. I know my own hand.
lines.speak: I never wrote that line. I know my own hand.

lines.speaker: SALIM
lines.text: A van. At this hour.
lines.speak: A van. At this hour.

lines.speaker: NIKHIL
lines.text: Four tapes, a hundred and fifty rupees. The man didn't even look up when I paid.
lines.speak: Four tapes, a hundred and fifty rupees. The man didn't even look up when I paid.

lines.speaker: NIKHIL
lines.text: A watchman. Some housing society in '98. Whoever filmed that never stopped the camera.
lines.speak: A watchman. Some housing society in '98. Whoever filmed that never stopped the camera.

lines.speaker: NIKHIL
lines.text: The van in that tape was white too. Same as... no. Lots of white vans.
lines.speak: The van in that tape was white too. Same as... no. Lots of white vans.

lines.speaker: NIKHIL
lines.text: Room 108. Why do I know that number?
lines.speak: Room 108. Why do I know that number?

lines.speaker: NIKHIL
lines.text: Every address on that wall was crossed out. Except the last one.
lines.speak: Every address on that wall was crossed out. Except the last one.

lines.speaker: NIKHIL
lines.text: Same as the first one. No label. Just... waiting.
lines.speak: Same as the first one. No label. Just... waiting.

lines.speaker: NIKHIL
lines.text: Maa would say I eat like a hostel boy. She'd be right.
lines.speak: Maa would say I eat like a hostel boy. She'd be right.

lines.speaker: NIKHIL
lines.text: Twelve percent. I charged it this morning. Did I fall asleep with the tape running?
lines.speak: Twelve percent. I charged it this morning. Did I fall asleep with the tape running?

lines.speaker: NIKHIL
lines.text: It's almost one. I didn't order anything.
lines.speak: It's almost one. I didn't order anything.

lines.speaker: Vendor
lines.text: Purane video tapes. Dedh sau, poora dabba.  (Old video tapes. 150 for the whole box.)
lines.speak: Purane video tapes. Dedh sau, poora dabba.

lines.speaker: Vendor
lines.text: Le jao. Wapas mat lana.  (Take it. Don't bring it back.)
lines.speak: Le jao. Wapas mat lana.

lines.speaker: RAGHU
lines.text: 3:12. Exactly when he said.
lines.speak: 3:12. Exactly when he said.

lines.speaker: RAGHU (V.O.)
lines.text: The lights came back. All of them, all at once.
lines.speak: The lights came back. All of them, all at once.

lines.speaker: RAGHU (V.O.)
lines.text: The CCTV kept recording. The last frame from CAM 4 shows me at the board.
lines.speak: The CCTV kept recording. The last frame from CAM 4 shows me at the board.

lines.speaker: RAGHU (V.O.)
lines.text: And behind me, a small red light.
lines.speak: And behind me, a small red light.

lines.speaker: RAGHU (V.O.)
lines.text: The register says I signed out at six. I never signed out.
lines.speak: The register says I signed out at six. I never signed out.

lines.speaker: RAGHU
lines.text: Hello? Hello, 4B?
lines.speak: Hello? Hello, 4B?

lines.speaker: RAGHU
lines.text: [i](slow breathing)[/i]
lines.speak: (slow breathing)

lines.speaker: RAGHU
lines.text: Deshmukh-ji? Is that you? Sahab?
lines.speak: Deshmukh-ji? Is that you? Sahab?

lines.speaker: RAGHU (V.O.)
lines.text: Somebody had to go up and look. That was my job.
lines.speak: Somebody had to go up and look. That was my job.

lines.speaker: SALIM
lines.text: Exact change. Again.
lines.speak: Exact change. Again.

lines.speaker: SALIM
lines.text: ...That's my name.
lines.speak: ...That's my name.

lines.speaker: SALIM (V.O.)
lines.text: They found the booth empty at six. The arm was up. The cash tray was full of exact change.
lines.speak: They found the booth empty at six. The arm was up. The cash tray was full of exact change.

lines.speaker: MAA
lines.text: Hello? Beta? Awaaz aa rahi hai?
lines.speak: Hello? Beta? Awaaz aa rahi hai?

lines.speaker: MAA
lines.text: (Can you hear me?)
lines.speak: (Can you hear me?)

lines.speaker: NIKHIL
lines.text: Haan Maa. Bolo.
lines.speak: Haan Maa. Bolo.

lines.speaker: MAA
lines.text: Kaam kaam kaam. Aankhen dekho apni. Video call pe dikhti hain.
lines.speak: Kaam kaam kaam. Aankhen dekho apni. Video call pe dikhti hain.

lines.speaker: MAA
lines.text: Teen baje? Main toh dus baje so jaati hoon, beta. Tumne kiya hoga.
lines.speak: Teen baje? Main toh dus baje so jaati hoon, beta. Tumne kiya hoga.

lines.speaker: MAA
lines.text: (At three? I'm asleep by ten. You must have called.)
lines.speak: (At three? I'm asleep by ten. You must have called.)

lines.speaker: MAA
lines.text: Achha, so jao. Sunday ko phone karna. Papa bhi baat karenge.
lines.speak: Achha, so jao. Sunday ko phone karna. Papa bhi baat karenge.

lines.speaker: MR. DESHMUKH
lines.text: You must be Raghu.
lines.speak: You must be Raghu.

lines.speaker: MR. DESHMUKH
lines.text: It's written on your face, beta. Like it was on Kishan's.
lines.speak: It's written on your face, beta. Like it was on Kishan's.

lines.speaker: MR. DESHMUKH
lines.text: Deshmukh. 4B. I have been here longer than these walls.
lines.speak: Deshmukh. 4B. I have been here longer than these walls.

lines.speaker: MR. DESHMUKH
lines.text: I take a small walk at three. Kishan kept the little gate open for me. You will also, no?
lines.speak: I take a small walk at three. Kishan kept the little gate open for me. You will also, no?

lines.speaker: MR. DESHMUKH
lines.text: Out. I always come back.
lines.speak: Out. I always come back.

lines.speaker: MR. DESHMUKH
lines.text: Good boy. Three-twelve. Don't be late.
lines.speak: Good boy. Three-twelve. Don't be late.

lines.speaker: MR. DESHMUKH
lines.text: Locks. Kishan also had locks.
lines.speak: Locks. Kishan also had locks.

lines.speaker: MR. DESHMUKH
lines.text: Goodnight, Raghu.
lines.speak: Goodnight, Raghu.

lines.speaker: MR. DESHMUKH
lines.text: Since the foundation stone. My wife chose 4B for the morning light.
lines.speak: Since the foundation stone. My wife chose 4B for the morning light.

lines.speaker: MR. DESHMUKH
lines.text: She is gone now. The light still comes. Every morning, for nobody.
lines.speak: She is gone now. The light still comes. Every morning, for nobody.

lines.speaker: MR. DESHMUKH
lines.text: Kishan stopped asking questions. That was good of him.
lines.speak: Kishan stopped asking questions. That was good of him.

lines.speaker: MR. DESHMUKH
lines.text: You ask a lot of questions, Raghu.
lines.speak: You ask a lot of questions, Raghu.

lines.speaker: MRS. IYER
lines.text: Arre, the new watchman? Good, good. Iyer, 2C. A courier came for me in the evening, no?
lines.speak: Arre, the new watchman? Good, good. Iyer, 2C. A courier came for me in the evening, no?

lines.speaker: MRS. IYER
lines.text: So? My parcel?
lines.speak: So? My parcel?

lines.speaker: MRS. IYER
lines.text: It'll be in the cabin. Kishan always kept them on the floor by the window.
lines.speak: It'll be in the cabin. Kishan always kept them on the floor by the window.

lines.speaker: MRS. IYER
lines.text: Nice man. Last week he started sitting with that CCTV all night. Said someone on the D wing terrace was filming him.
lines.speak: Nice man. Last week he started sitting with that CCTV all night. Said someone on the D wing terrace was filming him.

lines.speaker: MRS. IYER
lines.text: Then one morning his chair was empty. Anyway.
lines.speak: Then one morning his chair was empty. Anyway.

lines.speaker: MRS. IYER
lines.text: Thank you, beta.
lines.speak: Thank you, beta.

lines.speaker: MRS. IYER
lines.text: And tell the man on the D wing terrace to switch off his little red light. It blinks right into my bedroom.
lines.speak: And tell the man on the D wing terrace to switch off his little red light. It blinks right into my bedroom.

lines.speaker: MRS. IYER
lines.text: Then who keeps waving at me?
lines.speak: Then who keeps waving at me?

lines.speaker: MRS. IYER
lines.text: Good. Goodnight, beta.
lines.speak: Good. Goodnight, beta.

lines.speaker: MRS. IYER
lines.text: Go, go. Do your rounds. And that red light, okay?
lines.speak: Go, go. Do your rounds. And that red light, okay?

lines.speaker: MRS. IYER
lines.text: Who sleeps at my age? Since my husband passed, I keep the TV on for the noise.
lines.speak: Who sleeps at my age? Since my husband passed, I keep the TV on for the noise.

lines.speaker: MRS. IYER
lines.text: Sun TV, all night. Even the static is company. Anyway.
lines.speak: Sun TV, all night. Even the static is company. Anyway.

lines.speaker: SECRETARY
lines.text: Hello? ...Who is this, at this hour?
lines.speak: Hello? ...Who is this, at this hour?

lines.speaker: SECRETARY
lines.text: Raghu. I know it's you. Speak.
lines.speak: Raghu. I know it's you. Speak.

lines.speaker: RAGHU
lines.text: Mr. Deshmukh from 4B went out at 3:12. He hasn't come back. And the intercom from 4B...
lines.speak: Mr. Deshmukh from 4B went out at 3:12. He hasn't come back. And the intercom from 4B...

lines.speaker: SECRETARY
lines.text: You let him out? Kishan said the same thing. Kishan also kept a gate open.
lines.speak: You let him out? Kishan said the same thing. Kishan also kept a gate open.

lines.speaker: SECRETARY
lines.text: Deshmukh? From 4B?
lines.speak: Deshmukh? From 4B?

lines.speaker: SECRETARY
lines.text: Raghu, 4B has been empty for eight months. Deshmukh-ji left in July.
lines.speak: Raghu, 4B has been empty for eight months. Deshmukh-ji left in July.

lines.speaker: SECRETARY
lines.text: On the camera.
lines.speak: On the camera.

lines.speaker: SECRETARY
lines.text: Is it recording now? The camera?
lines.speak: Is it recording now? The camera?

lines.speaker: SECRETARY
lines.text: Nobody. That line is dead. I had it cut in August.
lines.speak: Nobody. That line is dead. I had it cut in August.

lines.speaker: SECRETARY
lines.text: Mrs. Iyer has called me about that light every night since July.
lines.speak: Mrs. Iyer has called me about that light every night since July.

lines.speaker: RAGHU
lines.text: Sahab? Hello—
lines.speak: Sahab? Hello—

lines.speaker: SALIM
lines.text: Booth three to control. Pillai sir?
lines.speak: Booth three to control. Pillai sir?

lines.speaker: PILLAI (RADIO)
lines.text: Control. Go ahead, Salim.
lines.speak: Control. Go ahead, Salim.

lines.speaker: PILLAI (RADIO)
lines.text: Good. Trucks start after four. Till then, don't sleep, and log every plate. Every plate.
lines.speak: Good. Trucks start after four. Till then, don't sleep, and log every plate. Every plate.

lines.speaker: SALIM
lines.text: Every plate. Over.
lines.speak: Every plate. Over.

lines.speaker: SALIM
lines.text: Control? Pillai sir? Booth three. Please answer.
lines.speak: Control? Pillai sir? Booth three. Please answer.

lines.speaker: SALIM
lines.text: [i](static)[/i]
lines.speak: (static)

lines.speaker: SALIM
lines.text: Sir, the van. It came back again. There were more people in it.
lines.speak: Sir, the van. It came back again. There were more people in it.

lines.speaker: RADIO
lines.text: ...Booth three. Salim bhai. Who is that sitting with you?
lines.speak: ...Booth three. Salim bhai. Who is that sitting with you?

lines.speaker: SALIM
lines.text: [i](the static stops)[/i]
lines.speak: (the static stops)

lines.speaker: SALIM
lines.text: Control, booth three. Sir, a white Omni just went through. Bombay plate.
lines.speak: Control, booth three. Sir, a white Omni just went through. Bombay plate.

lines.speaker: PILLAI (RADIO)
lines.text: Omni? I've had your lane camera up the whole time, Salim. Nothing has gone through booth three in an hour.
lines.speak: Omni? I've had your lane camera up the whole time, Salim. Nothing has gone through booth three in an hour.

lines.speaker: PILLAI (RADIO)
lines.text: Then count it again. And stop calling me about ghosts.
lines.speak: Then count it again. And stop calling me about ghosts.

lines.speaker: PILLAI (RADIO)
lines.text: Then go wash your face. Two more hours.
lines.speak: Then go wash your face. Two more hours.

lines.speaker: SALIM
lines.text: Yes, sir. Over.
lines.speak: Yes, sir. Over.
